title: introduce-tenant-budget-agent-mini-batcher-and-telemetry-bridge
author: Marisol Garza
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware budget agent that adjusts mini-batcher sizing and cache hints based on unit-econ signals; bridges cost telemetry to Console for per-tenant budgeting insights.
description:
Context: Some tenants (especially low-traffic, budget-constrained customers) are seeing unpredictable unit economics due to static batching/cache defaults and one-size quantization profiles. This led to customer tickets where a small change in request pattern caused a disproportionate cost spike.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight tenant budget agent plus a mini-batcher runtime hook and a telemetry bridge so: (1) tenants can have conservative, tenant-scoped batching/cache defaults that optimize cost without violating latency SLOs; (2) operators can see per-tenant cost signals in Console and tie them to recommended batch/cache/quant settings; (3) runtime can apply safe, reversible adjustments with clear audit trails.

What this PR does: Single continuous change split into small commits (see list below) that together:  - add services/budget-agent: a sidecar service that consumes sampling telemetry (qps, p50/p95 token counts, cost-per-token estimate) and exposes a decision API for per-tenant profiles;  - add runtime/mini-batcher hook: a low-risk, per-request hook that can switch between micro-batching strategies (zero/low/high) and adjust prefix cache hints returned from the agent;  - add telemetry/bridge: transforms budget-agent decisions and unit-econ signals into Console ingest events and a lightweight metrics facade (tenant_budget{policy,score,applied});  - wire rollout flags, canary config and safety gates to ensure we never widen latency SLOs.

Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (Linear ENG-2043) [x] unit tests for decision logic [x] integration tests for mini-batcher fallback path [x] end-to-end smoke in staging [x] Console dashboard (telemetry) skeleton [x] production rollout plan (canary to 5 tenants -> 50 -> 500)

Commits (high level):  - a1b2c3: initial budget-agent skeleton, config, and proto for decision API  - d4e5f6: implement scoring model (traffic-weighted unit-econ + safety margin)  - 9f8e7d: mini-batcher runtime hook and local fallback policy  - c3b2a1: telemetry bridge and metrics serializer  - b7a6c5: tests + integration harness and basic docs  - f0e1d2: rollout gates, feature flags and canary automation scripts

Changed areas (high-level):  - services/budget-agent/*  - runtime/batcher/mini_batcher.go  - runtime/batcher/mini_batcher_test.go  - runtime/cache/prefix_hints.go  - telemetry/bridge/transformer.go  - console/dashboards/tenant_budget_overview.json  - infra/helm/budget-agent-chart.yaml  - docs/ops/budget-agent.md  - examples/samples/tenant-budget-policy.yaml

Design notes and safety: The agent uses only sampled telemetry (1 in N requests) to avoid telemetry explosion. Decisions are conservative: adjustments are bounded and must either improve unit-econ score by a configurable delta or be reverted by the safety gate. All changes are recorded in an audit log and surfaced to Console. The mini-batcher hook defaults to NO-OP unless a tenant profile is present (opt-in via tenant annotation). Fallback path: if the decision API is unreachable or returns an error, the runtime uses the pre-existing per-tenant config.

Testing and CI: Local unit/integration tests added. CI ran full unit suite and the mini-batcher integration matrix. We observed a flaky test (batcher/scheduling_test.go) in first run; retried and all checks passed.

Rollout plan: feature flag controlled; start with canary = 5 tenants (low qps), monitor token cost delta in Console and p99 latency; if stable after 72h, ramp to 50 tenants, then 500. If the safety gate trips (cost up > 10% or p99 latency up > 5%), automatic rollback and alert to oncall.

Why unique: Rather than only suggesting static defaults or global heuristics, this change introduces a small decision agent that ties telemetry to runtime controls and Console visibility, enabling tenant-aware conservative optimization that is reversible and auditable.

Merge: Squash-merged by Dmitri Kovalev after 2 approvals and green CI.
discussion: 2026-02-14 - Dmitri Kovalev: Overall looks good. Two design questions: how often does the agent poll telemetry and how do we bound oscillation?
